model_description: Descriptive shot-make probability model for NBA simulator (Phase 4a). Baseline Model A fitted on regular-play shots only; Model B adds shrunk per-player regular-play offsets; optional clutch shift adds a descriptive constant logit-scale offset estimated from clutch out-of-fold residuals.

feature_rules.loc_units: LOC_X and LOC_Y are in tenths of a foot with the hoop at (0, 0).
feature_rules.shot_distance_ft: Computed as hypot(LOC_X, LOC_Y) / 10.0 when not explicitly supplied.
feature_rules.shot_angle: Computed as degrees(arctan2(LOC_X, LOC_Y)) when not explicitly supplied.
feature_rules.is_putback: 1 if ACTION_TYPE contains 'tip' or 'putback' (case-insensitive), else 0, unless IS_PUTBACK is provided explicitly.
feature_rules.distance_clamp_rule: If IS_PUTBACK == 0 and SHOT_DISTANCE_FT < 1.0, clamp SHOT_DISTANCE_FT to 1.0 (matches src/predict.py; in training data, exact (0, 0) occurs almost only on tips and putbacks).
feature_rules.unknown_action_group_policy: Raise ValueError if any ACTION_GROUP value is not in action_group_categories.

prediction_formula.model_b: p_B = clip(p_A + b_player, 0.01, 0.99); unknown/absent player uses b_player = 0 so p_B = p_A
prediction_formula.final: p_final = sigmoid(logit(clip(p_base, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)) + shift), with shift = 0 when clutch_shift=False

player_offsets.estimator: DerSimonian-Laird empirical-Bayes shrinkage on REGULAR OOF residuals (Model A)
player_offsets.absent_player_rule: The 10 players with no regular-play shots (plus any unknown player) are absent from player_offsets.csv and receive offset 0.0.

limitations: Single season only (2025-26 NBA regular season).
No defender tracking, closest-defender distance, or shot-clock data.
The clutch shift is a descriptive gap, not a causal pressure effect; it bundles defensive intensity, fatigue, shot selection within shot type, and shooter composition.
The clutch shift was estimated using out-of-fold p_A/p_B from models trained on 80% of games, whereas the exported Model A is fitted on 100% of regular-play shots (a second-order difference).

Player offsets in the export are estimated from all regular-play shots using out-of-fold residuals, so players with few shots are shrunk more toward the grand mean, and the 10 players with zero regular-play shots are absent from player_offsets.csv and receive offset 0.0.
